Sex-linked pedigrees and testing a model

A row of eight dogs with contrasting ear positions, coat textures and body outlines.

Genotype and phenotype chart: BB, labelled homozygous dominant, produces a purple flower; Bb, labelled heterozygous, also produces a purple flower; bb, labelled homozygous recessive, produces a white flower.

Six pea-plant contrasts: long and short stems; purple and white flowers; round and wrinkled seeds; yellow and green seeds; green and yellow pods; inflated and pinched pods. The seed-colour drawing places yellow on the left and green on the right, although its caption lists green first.

Seed-shape sequence with a round and a wrinkled P parent, an all-round F1 generation, and an F2 generation showing round and wrinkled seeds. The drawing labels the schematic F2 proportions three quarters round and one quarter wrinkled and describes crosses between F1 plants.

A meiosis schematic with two homologous chromosome pairs, distinguished by length, and two possible arrangements. In each arrangement, copied X-shaped homologues separate into two cells; sister chromatids later separate into single chromosome rods. For this lesson, follow only the long blue and long red chromosomes in the left-hand arrangement.

A true-breeding round parent labelled RR is crossed with a true-breeding wrinkled parent labelled rr. Arrows lead to a round F1 seed category labelled Rr and 100 percent of offspring. The drawing abbreviates the gamete and fertilisation steps.

A two-by-two Punnett square with R and r across the top and R and r down the left. The four interior entries are RR, Rr, Rr and rr. In the accompanying explanation, top entries are sperm contributions and left entries are egg contributions.
A black-furred mouse, used to illustrate the black coat category in the stated model.
A brown-furred mouse, used to illustrate the contrasting brown coat category in the stated model.

Two fully visible single-trait squares. The left has B and B across the top and b and b down the left, giving four Bb cells. The right has B and b across the top and b and b down the left, giving Bb and bb in each row.
Each row and column represents a gamete. Four equally likely combinations give a 1:2:1 genotype ratio under the stated model. A is completely dominant to a.
Two black-mouse photographs at the top connect by plain converging lines to one black-mouse photograph in the middle. A vertical line leads from the middle photograph to a question mark below.

A tall pea plant on the left and a short plant beside it, with a separate upper-right inset showing a green pod on the left and a yellow pod on the right.
The chosen P plants: a tall plant with green pods on the left crossed with a short plant with yellow pods on the right. Boxed pod details enlarge the colour contrast.
Combination arrows around TTGG give TG, TG, TG, TG. Arrows around ttgg give tg, tg, tg, tg. Each repeated list contains only one distinct gamete type.
An expanded P-cross grid repeats TG in all four columns and tg in all four rows. Every cell is TtGg. Its annotation identifies all F1 offspring as heterozygous at both loci, tall with green pods.

The complete TtGg by TtGg F2 grid has TG, Tg, tG and tg on both edges. Green ovals mark nine tall green-pod cells, yellow ovals three tall yellow-pod cells, green rectangles three short green-pod cells, and a yellow rectangle one short yellow-pod cell. The 9:3:3:1 ratio is already printed at right.

Two alternative orientations of long and short homologous chromosome pairs. The long pair retains its arrangement while the short pair reverses. Homologues separate into the middle cells, labelled Metaphase II; sisters then separate, producing four labelled chromosome-combination types across the two alternatives.
Follow each branch from AaBb through one allele at the first locus and one at the second. Each endpoint is one haploid gamete, with probability one quarter.

A red R1R1 flower and a white R2R2 flower at the top are joined by a cross sign. Arrows from both lead to a pink R1R2 flower below. The diagram abbreviates reproduction between the parent and offspring levels.

A blue-roan horse with a mixed grey-blue body, dark mane and lower legs, and a white facial marking. Original copyright and photographer text remain visible. The coat illustration supports a comparison of an intermixed body coat with darker regions.

An illustration of red, disc-shaped blood cells within a vessel. No A or B molecular markers or blood-group labels are resolved in the image, so it cannot identify the cells' ABO types.
The standard three-allele ABO model produces four possible offspring genotypes in this cross. Each letter marks one phenotype to infer from its genotype.

The cross IAIA × IBi appears above a square. IA is repeated in both top columns. The left rows are IB and i. The upper cells are both IAIB and the lower cells both IAi. Repeated IA columns represent one distinct egg allele type.

Genotype-to-phenotype table for the stated X-linked recessive colour-vision model. XX genotypes XB XB and XB Xb are labelled regular vision; Xb Xb is labelled colour blind. XY genotypes XB Y and Xb Y are labelled regular vision and colour blind respectively.
A cat with orange and black patches across its head and body, and white fur around the muzzle and paws. The photograph shows patches, not chromosomes or the cat's measured genotype.

Figure 17.24. Panel A is an AaBb by AaBb square grouping offspring into five additive ear-length categories. Panel B has five bars in the ratio 1, 4, 6, 4, 1 from shortest to longest. Panel C extends the simplified model to three loci and seven categories with relative heights 1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1. Curves connect the distributions schematically.
In this fully penetrant autosomal recessive model, filled symbols are affected. Unaffected parents with an affected child must both be carriers. The unaffected sibling remains AA or Aa.

Autosomal-dominant pedigree numbered 1 through 12. Affected parents 1 and 2 have affected children 5 and 6 and unaffected child 7. Unaffected 3 and affected 4 have unaffected 8 and affected 9. Unaffected 7 and 8 have unaffected children 10, 11 and 12.

Three-generation pedigree. Two unaffected parents have an unaffected daughter, an affected son, an unaffected son and another unaffected daughter. The left daughter and her unaffected partner have an unaffected daughter and two unaffected sons. The right daughter and her unaffected partner have an affected son and two unaffected daughters.

X-linked-dominant pedigree numbered 1 through 11. Affected mother 1 and unaffected father 2 have affected son 3, affected daughter 4, unaffected son 5 and unaffected daughter 6. Unaffected daughter 6 and affected partner 7 have affected daughters 8 and 10 and unaffected sons 9 and 11.

An affected mother and unaffected father have two affected children, a son and daughter, and two unaffected children, a son and daughter. The affected son and an unaffected female partner have an affected son. The unaffected daughter and an unaffected male partner have an unaffected daughter. The diagram asks for the mode of inheritance.
The starting arrangement is AB/ab. Without crossing over, AB and ab are parental combinations; Ab and aB are recombinants.

A prophase-I tetrad starts with two blue AB chromatids and two red ab chromatids. One blue and one red nonsister chromatid exchange the segment between the A and B loci. After the two meiotic divisions, the four daughter-cell products are AB, Ab, aB and ab; the two middle products are recombinant.

Two homologous chromosomes carry three corresponding loci. The upper blue locus is labelled B on the left and b on the right; a lower purple locus is H and h; a nearby green locus is d and D. The H-to-d interval is drawn shorter than the B-to-H interval.
The schematic positions are 0, 8 and 20 cM. The middle locus is 8 cM from the left locus and 12 cM from the right locus; the total map interval is 20 cM.
